authors: T.W. Bartel; S.L. Yaniv
title: Creep and creep recovery response of load cells tested according to US and international evaluation procedures
observation: Across 65 load cells examined using NTEP test data, the mean ratio of maximum absolute creep recovery to maximum absolute creep is 0.86. The average ratio of 30-minute to 60-minute creep is 0.84. Unloading history informs the shape of a zero-point recovery trial.
limitation: Population summaries do not identify an individual cell’s correction. Uniaxial force test without contact mechanics or six-axis wrist channels.
rights: NIST-hosted journal PDF. Link and original summary.

authors: Paula Weidinger; Gisa Foyer; Stefan Kock; Jonas Gnauert; Rolf Kumme
title: Calibration of torque measurement under constant rotation in a wind turbine test bench
locator: Sections 2.2 and 5.3; Fig. 9 and uncertainty table
observation: Torque transfer standard at a 4 MW wind-turbine test bench. Heating-blanket calibration compared 20.85 and 32.77 °C internal temperature. In-rotation shaft records varied by about ±2 K over a day and ±1 K during a 60 min cycle. Temperature contribution to relative uncertainty was 0.0152%.
limitation: Internal air served as a proxy for solid temperature during test bench calibration. Magnitudes from a MN·m system are not wrist coefficients.
rights: CC BY 4.0 per publisher.

authors: Andreas Brüge; Harald Pfeiffer
title: A Standard for Rotatory Power Measurement
locator: Sections on idling torque and temperature; Table 1
observation: In the PTB rotating power standard, the open shaft is rotated at medium speed to determine idling torque and correct offset. Estimated thermal contribution to the torque sensitivity term is 1.4×10^-5 for a possible 5 K temperature change.
limitation: The temperature contribution uses a typical coefficient in an uncertainty calculation. It is not a five-degree raw warming trace.
rights: Article identifies Creative Commons Attribution 3.0.

authors: J. Fidelus; K. Cybul
title: Study on short-term creep effect and hysteresis for the HBM Z4A force transducer under compressive and tensile forces
observation: GUM deadweight tests on an HBM Z4A compare loading and unloading under tension and compression. Short-time creep can reverse near the third second after loading. The higher relative hysteresis error changes from compression at loads up to 5 kN to tension in the 5–30 kN range.
limitation: Single selected sensor and axial standard. Polarity and time-after-step influence the outcome. No six-axis or synchronized temperature record.
rights: Public Acta IMEKO paper. Link and factual summaries.

authors: Georg Wegener; Werner Nold; Jürgen Andrae; Kai Molitor
title: Measurement uncertainty of rotating torque transducers when used in partial load ranges
observation: Partial-load calibration changes how hysteresis, nonlinearity and zero return enter the uncertainty budget. Table 5 explicitly rejects scaling zero return from the full calibration span to a smaller span.
limitation: Manufacturer case examples. This is an uncertainty analysis, not a temperature experiment or timestamped data release.
rights: Public IMEKO proceedings. Reuse terms for source files were not verified. Link, citation and self-computed factual summaries only.

authors: Min-Seok Kim; Mulugeta Derebew; Yon-Kyu Park
title: Simultaneous determination of temperature and humidity sensitivity coefficients of torque transfer standards in ambient conditions
observation: Ambient-condition regression on two 1000 N·m torque transfer standards finds temperature terms of 7.9×10^-5 and 9.4×10^-6 per °C. The humidity coefficients have opposite signs: +4.2×10^-7 and −1.0×10^-6 per percentage point RH.
limitation: Fitted coefficients from naturally varying ambient conditions, with uncertainty in Table 1. Do not equate independent drift excitations or extrapolate to wrist sensors.
rights: Public IMEKO proceedings. Reuse terms for source files were not verified. Link, citation and self-computed factual summaries only.

authors: Laurence Brice; Andy Knott; Alan Wilson
title: Continuous calibration of force transducers
observation: Compared continuous ramp calibration against a serial reference and conventional static calibration on four force transducers. Output agreement is within 0.05% in the study. Figure 5 presents creep during a constant-load period.
limitation: Ramp rate, transducer type and capture system constrain transfer. The measured creep is a held mechanical load response.
rights: Public IMEKO proceedings. Reuse terms for source files were not verified. Link, citation and self-computed factual summaries only.

authors: K. M. Khaled; D. Röske
title: The influence of temperature and humidity on the creep of torque transducers
observation: Instrument-specific contrasts from the controlled 22→40→22 °C and 50→70→50% RH sequences separate loaded creep and recovery after unloading at 3 and 30 min. At 22 °C, increasing RH raised 30-min creep for TT1#37102-03 by 0.000035 mV/V but lowered it for T34-R40#607101 by 0.000093 mV/V.
limitation: Opposite humidity slopes within Table 2 qualify the general direction stated in the conclusion. Tables are plateau summaries with uncertainties. No raw traces or six-axis robot measurements.
rights: Public IMEKO proceedings. Reuse terms for source files were not verified. Link, citation and self-computed factual summaries only.

authors: Andreas Brüge
title: Creep measurement in reference torque calibration machines
observation: On one 100 N·m reference transducer, clockwise short-term unloading creep in units of 10^-4 is −1.5 under direct deadweight, −3.1 using the drive and −3.0 under hand loading. Release method and preceding load sequence affect apparent recovery.
limitation: Methods also differ in load application history. Single numerical example does not isolate a universal correction.
rights: Public IMEKO proceedings. Reuse terms for source files were not verified. Link, citation and self-computed factual summaries only.

authors: Ebtisam H. Hasan; Günther Haucke; Rolf Kumme
title: Effect of different loading schemes on creep and creep recovery for force measurements
observation: At maximum capacity, direct-loading creep strictly exceeds both partial-step and full-step creep for five of the seven force transducer rows. The exceptions are A–100 kN and A–200 N.
limitation: These are instrument comparisons at one interval, not repeated independent wrist trials. Calculated from the seven printed triples.
rights: Public IMEKO proceedings. Reuse terms for source files were not verified. Link, citation and self-computed factual summaries only.

authors: Andreas Brüge
title: Fast torque calibrations using continuous procedures
observation: Continuous versus stepped torque calibration demonstrates sensitivity to loading history and time alignment. The reference-creep contribution is explored with a simulation; trigger instability can add spikes to matching curves.
limitation: Published calibration examples and simulation must be distinguished. No physical actuator saturation or six-axis trace.
rights: Public IMEKO proceedings. Reuse terms for source files were not verified. Link, citation and self-computed factual summaries only.

authors: Younghee Han; Raymond A. de Callafon
title: Output error identification of closed-loop Hammerstein systems
observation: Two simulated closed-loop Hammerstein cases use known controller/reference information. Case 2 substitutes a saturating static nonlinearity. Figure 4 reports the identified map and dynamic frequency response.
limitation: Simulation only. A known stable feedback design and chosen excitation are assumptions. Does not verify measured plant-side clipping or anti-windup performance.
rights: IEEE conference copyright. Public proceedings PDF, links and summary only.

authors: Younghee Han; Raymond A. de Callafon
title: Closed-loop Identification of Hammerstein Systems Using Iterative Instrumental Variables
locator: Section 5, Application to LTO-3 tape drive; Figs. 4–6
observation: Measured closed-loop LTO-3 servo: 1,406,251 position-error samples at 20 kHz, known controller and ±5 V actuator limit. Figure 4 separates measured controller command u and output y from internal x after saturation. Figure 6 compares measured signals with model simulation.
limitation: N=10,000 and “0.05 sec” are both printed. At 20 kHz these samples span about 0.5 s; retain this unresolved conflict. The plotted post-limit signal is simulated. No downloadable experiment log was verified.
rights: IFAC conference copyright. Free full PDF, no data reuse grant verified.

authors: Younghee Han
title: Block-oriented nonlinear system identification using semidefinite programming
source_version: UC San Diego dissertation PDF, eScholarship
observation: The dissertation reports the LTO-3 ±5 V physical experiment, simulation, and identification assumptions together. Section 6.7 explicitly names the IFAC and CDC papers as sources for Chapter 6.
limitation: Same experiment family as the IFAC paper. Does not supply an independent replication, a post-limiter voltage log or a standalone dataset.
rights: UC eScholarship public author dissertation. Copyright retained.

authors: Shudong Zhuang; Wen Yang; Yuxiang Zhou; Ying Zou; Chang Liu; Le Zhang; Miao Tong; Jinlong Ma
title: Temperature field analysis and compensation improvement of load cell
observation: Finite element position selection is checked in a chamber at −10, 20 and 40 °C, with PT1000 probes at different positions. The experimental comparison assesses variation in temperature difference to the strain-gauge region; the author reports position 2 is most stable.
limitation: Temperature difference stability does not directly measure corrected output-force error. Position numbering varies in the methods prose. Data are available from the author upon reasonable request.
rights: Publisher CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Link and independent factual summary.

authors: Jumpei Arata; Tatsuya Nitta; Toshiki Nakatsuka; Tomonori Kawabata; Tadao Matsunaga; Yoichi Haga; Kanako Harada; Mamoru Mitsuishi
title: Modular Optic Force Sensor for a Surgical Device Using a Fabry–Perot Interferometer
observation: A Fabry–Perot sensor shows wavelength temperature gains of 2.36 nm/°C alone and 2.61 nm/°C when mounted. Its separate applied-force calibration gives 2.52 nm/N. The isolated-sensor gains imply an apparent 0.94 N/°C for this comparison.
limitation: The ratio is a derived scale check from separate tests. A temperature ramp is not an actual applied load. Not a six-axis wrist sensor.
rights: CC BY 4.0 per publisher.

authors: Arnaldo Leal-Junior; Antreas Theodosiou; Camilo Díaz; Carlos Marques; Maria José Pontes; Kyriacos Kalli; Anselmo Frizera-Neto
title: Fiber Bragg Gratings in CYTOP Fibers Embedded in a 3D-Printed Flexible Support for Assessment of Human–Robot Interaction Forces
observation: A CYTOP FBG shank support was characterized for load, temperature, and creep under constant load. Correcting temperature and creep separately produces reported validation-force errors between 0.50 and 2.29 N.
limitation: Optical orthosis support. These are reported extrema across validation cases, not a six-axis wrist bias estimate.
rights: CC BY 4.0 per publisher.

authors: Xingchi He; James Handa; Peter Gehlbach; Russell Taylor; Iulian Iordachita
title: A Submillimetric 3-DOF Force Sensing Instrument With Integrated Fiber Bragg Grating for Retinal Microsurgery
observation: Temperature compensation on a 3-DOF optical tool is calibrated during unloaded-tip heating/cooling (roughly ten minutes each). With fitted coefficient 0.43, validation against a scale and spring in the axial direction yielded 0.92 mN RMS error.
limitation: Optical axial/lateral channels and mN loads on a microsurgical prototype. Reference spring scale and temperature trial have different roles.
rights: IEEE author manuscript via PMC. No blanket redistribution of the manuscript or underlying data assumed.

authors: Berk Gonenc; Alireza Chamani; James Handa; Peter Gehlbach; Russell H. Taylor; Iulian Iordachita
title: 3-DOF Force-Sensing Motorized Micro-Forceps for Robot-Assisted Vitreoretinal Surgery
observation: Four thermal characterization sessions of 225 min sampled every 15 min over ambient shifts of about ±2.5 °C and with different orientations. The authors report covariance of 0.94 between axial drift and the common mode of the lateral channels. The axial temperature coefficient fitted from these channels is 0.92.
limitation: A single optical micro-forceps prototype. Long-term temperature drift here follows wavelength channels, not torque channels.
rights: IEEE author manuscript via PMC. Source linked, no file redistribution.

authors: Omar Al-Ahmad; Mouloud Ourak; Johan Vlekken; Eric Lindner; Emmanuel Vander Poorten
title: Three-dimensional catheter tip force sensing using multi-core fiber Bragg gratings
observation: A 20–60 °C excursion in 10 °C steps was applied for two cycles, first under unloaded conditions and then repeated under a hanging load. Figure 7C reports compensated force errors within ±0.008 N.
limitation: Single prototype with unloaded calibration and loaded validation. The paper describes two complete cycles and repeats the procedure under load; exact count per plotted condition is not independently reconstructed. No wrist torque data.
rights: CC BY 4.0 per publisher.
